title: Code review breaks down when no human understands the generated change
friendlyTitle: Do not submit AI code that nobody understands
summary: Raed Abdallah argues that conventional code review assumes an accountable author who can explain a change, an assumption weakened when agents produce complete pull requests before a person understands them. He proposes a simple readiness rule: the submitting human must explain the intent, affected invariants and evidence that the change is safe.
friendlySummary: AI can create a complete code change before a person understands it. The article says the person submitting the work should explain what it does, what it may affect and why it is safe.
whyItMatters: Generating code faster does not generate organizational context or ownership. Teams can protect review quality by requiring human explanations, smaller changes, tests tied to risks and a named operator who can maintain what the agent produced.
friendlyWhyItMatters: A passing test is not enough if nobody can maintain the code later. Keep changes small and make a real person responsible for them.
